title: English Language Practice Guide
introduction: Build accuracy by combining grammar, vocabulary, comprehension, lexis and structure. After every practice session, review why each option is correct or incorrect. Use timed practice and review grammar rules after each set. For comprehension, answer from evidence in the passage rather than assumption.

topics.title: Grammar and Structure
topics.content: Revise concord, tenses, conditional sentences, reported speech, clauses, modifiers and punctuation. Pay attention to the exact relationship between subjects and verbs.

topics.title: Vocabulary
topics.content: Learn words in context rather than memorising isolated definitions. Practise synonyms, antonyms, idioms and words commonly confused.

topics.title: Comprehension
topics.content: Read the passage first for its central idea, then return to the relevant paragraph for evidence before choosing an option.

topics.title: Grammar
topics.content: Grammar: concord, tense, clauses, modifiers and punctuation.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: 20 questions timed, mark immediately, then record recurring errors.

title: Mathematics Practice Guide
introduction: Aim for method as well as the final answer. Write down formulas, substitute carefully and check units and signs before submitting. Build accuracy through worked examples and timed objective practice. Always show enough working to catch sign, unit and arithmetic errors.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.content: Practise linear equations, simultaneous equations, factorisation, indices and variation. Simplify each side systematically.

topics.title: Geometry and Mensuration
topics.content: Memorise standard area, volume, circle and triangle formulas. Draw a quick diagram when a problem describes a shape.

topics.title: Statistics and Probability
topics.content: Know mean, median, mode, range and basic probability. Express probability as favourable outcomes divided by total equally likely outcomes.

topics.title: Number and algebra
topics.content: Number and algebra: indices, logarithms, equations, inequalities, sequences and variation.

topics.title: Geometry and mensuration
topics.content: Geometry and mensuration: angles, polygons, circles, areas, volumes and scale drawings.

topics.title: Statistics and probability
topics.content: Statistics and probability: averages, tables, charts, probability and interpretation.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: solve without a calculator where appropriate, then verify calculations.

title: Biology Practice Guide
introduction: Study biology by connecting structures to their functions and processes to observable effects. Study biological processes as linked systems. Use labelled diagrams and explain why each process occurs, not just its definition.

topics.title: Cell Biology
topics.content: Know cell organelles, their functions, cell division, transport and differences between plant and animal cells.

topics.title: Nutrition and Transport
topics.content: Revise balanced diets, enzymes, digestion, blood components, circulation and transport in plants.

topics.title: Ecology
topics.content: Practise food chains, energy flow, population relationships, adaptation and environmental conservation.

topics.title: Cell biology
topics.content: Cell biology: cell structures, transport, enzymes, nutrition and respiration.

topics.title: Genetics and evolution
topics.content: Genetics and evolution: inheritance, variation, natural selection and population concepts.

topics.title: Human biology
topics.content: Human biology: nutrition, transport, excretion, reproduction, coordination and health.

title: Chemistry Practice Guide
introduction: Combine equations, observations and calculations. Always check chemical formulae, balancing and units. Combine equations, observations and calculations. Memorise common tests only after understanding the chemical reason for each observation.

topics.title: Atomic Structure
topics.content: Revise protons, neutrons, electrons, isotopes, electronic configuration and periodic trends.

topics.title: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics.content: Know indicators, pH, neutralisation and common methods of salt preparation.

topics.title: Organic Chemistry
topics.content: Learn homologous series, functional groups, naming, properties and common reactions of hydrocarbons and related compounds.

topics.title: Atomic structure and bonding
topics.content: Atomic structure and bonding: particles, electronic structure, ions and chemical formulae.

topics.title: Quantitative chemistry
topics.content: Quantitative chemistry: relative masses, mole calculations, concentration and gas relationships.

topics.title: Organic chemistry
topics.content: Organic chemistry: homologous series, functional groups, reactions and uses.

topics.title: Practical chemistry
topics.content: Practical chemistry: separation methods, tests for ions/gases, acids, bases and titration principles.

title: Physics Practice Guide
introduction: Physics questions often reward correct formula selection and careful unit conversion. Show the steps in calculations. Translate words into physical quantities, choose the correct formula, substitute with units and check whether the result is reasonable.

topics.title: Mechanics
topics.content: Practise speed, velocity, acceleration, force, work, energy, momentum and simple machines.

topics.title: Electricity
topics.content: Revise current, voltage, resistance, electrical power, series/parallel circuits and household safety.

topics.title: Waves and Optics
topics.content: Know wave properties, reflection, refraction, lenses, sound and the electromagnetic spectrum.

topics.title: Heat and waves
topics.content: Heat and waves: temperature, heat transfer, wave properties, sound and light.

topics.title: Electricity and magnetism
topics.content: Electricity and magnetism: current, voltage, resistance, circuits, electromagnetism and transformers.

topics.title: Practical skills
topics.content: Practical skills: graphs, measurements, significant figures, uncertainties and experimental precautions.

title: Government Practice Guide
introduction: Learn key political concepts with examples from constitutional government and civic institutions. Understand institutions and principles before memorising examples. Compare systems and explain the advantages and limitations of each.

topics.title: Constitutional Principles
topics.content: Revise rule of law, separation of powers, checks and balances, fundamental rights and constitutional amendment.

topics.title: Political Participation
topics.content: Study elections, political parties, pressure groups, public opinion and franchise.

topics.title: Institutions
topics.content: Know the functions and relationships of the legislature, executive, judiciary and electoral bodies.

topics.title: Constitutional government
topics.content: Constitutional government: constitutions, separation of powers, rule of law and checks and balances.

topics.title: Political participation
topics.content: Political participation: parties, pressure groups, public opinion, elections and electoral bodies.

topics.title: Systems of government
topics.content: Systems of government: presidential, parliamentary, federal, unitary and traditional institutions.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: answer comparison questions using definitions, features, examples and consequences.

title: Economics Practice Guide
introduction: Understand concepts through cause-and-effect relationships rather than memorising definitions alone. Draw simple diagrams where useful and distinguish between changes in demand/supply and movements along curves.

topics.title: Basic Economic Problems
topics.content: Revise scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, scale of preference and factors of production.

topics.title: Demand and Supply
topics.content: Practise shifts versus movements, equilibrium price, elasticity and factors affecting demand and supply.

topics.title: Macroeconomics
topics.content: Study inflation, unemployment, national income, money, banking and fiscal/monetary policy.

topics.title: Microeconomics
topics.content: Microeconomics: scarcity, opportunity cost, demand, supply, elasticity, production and market structures.

topics.title: International economics
topics.content: International economics: trade, exchange rates, balance of payments and development.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: define the concept, state the mechanism, then apply it to a realistic example.

title: Commerce Practice Guide
introduction: Focus on the functions of trade and the documents, institutions and services that support business. Learn commercial documents and functions by understanding the transaction they support. Practise distinguishing closely related terms.

topics.title: Trade
topics.content: Revise home and foreign trade, channels of distribution, wholesalers, retailers and auxiliaries to trade.

topics.title: Business Documents
topics.content: Know the purpose of invoices, receipts, quotations, orders, delivery notes, consignment notes and statements of account.

topics.title: Insurance and Finance
topics.content: Study principles of insurance, types of risk and the role of banks and other financial institutions.

topics.title: Aids to trade
topics.content: Aids to trade: banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication and advertising.

topics.title: Business organisations
topics.content: Business organisations: sole proprietorship, partnership, companies and cooperatives.

topics.title: Modern commerce
topics.content: Modern commerce: e-commerce, consumer protection, branding and business ethics.

title: Christian Religious Studies Guide
introduction: Read biblical passages in context and connect teachings with their moral and social implications. Study biblical narratives with attention to context, moral lessons and relationships between events. Avoid relying only on isolated quotations.

topics.title: Old Testament
topics.content: Revise creation, covenant, leadership, prophets, wisdom literature and major lessons from the lives of biblical figures.

topics.title: Life and Teachings of Jesus
topics.content: Study parables, miracles, teachings, death and resurrection, paying attention to the lessons conveyed.

topics.title: Early Church
topics.content: Revise Acts of the Apostles, the Holy Spirit, missionary work, leadership and challenges in the early church.

topics.title: Teachings of Jesus
topics.content: Teachings of Jesus: kingdom of God, love, forgiveness, service, faith and stewardship.

topics.title: Early church
topics.content: Early church: Acts, Christian fellowship, leadership, persecution and mission.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: identify the event, key characters, lesson and application before choosing an option.

title: Islamic Religious Knowledge Guide
introduction: Combine knowledge of Islamic beliefs and practices with the ethical principles they promote. Connect acts of worship with their ethical purposes. Study the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad alongside core Islamic principles.

topics.title: Five Pillars
topics.content: Revise Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, including their significance and basic requirements.

topics.title: Seerah
topics.content: Study major events in the life of Prophet Muhammad, including the Hijrah and the development of the Muslim community.

topics.title: Moral Conduct
topics.content: Practise questions on honesty, justice, charity, patience, family responsibility and peaceful relations.

topics.title: Qur’an and Sunnah
topics.content: Qur’an and Sunnah: revelation, guidance, moral conduct and sources of Islamic teaching.

topics.title: Islamic ethics
topics.content: Islamic ethics: honesty, justice, charity, family responsibilities and peaceful coexistence.

title: Financial Accounting Guide
introduction: Accounting becomes easier when you understand the effect of every transaction on assets, liabilities and capital. Master double-entry first, then apply it to books of original entry, ledgers, trial balance and final accounts.

topics.title: Double Entry
topics.content: Revise the rules of debit and credit and practise recording transactions in the appropriate accounts.

topics.title: Final Accounts
topics.content: Study trading, profit and loss accounts, balance sheets and adjustments such as depreciation and accruals.

topics.title: Control Procedures
topics.content: Revise trial balances, bank reconciliation, errors, suspense accounts and source documents.

topics.title: Double entry
topics.content: Double entry: debit/credit rules, accounting equation and source documents.

topics.title: Books and ledgers
topics.content: Books and ledgers: cash book, petty cash, sales/purchases books, returns and control accounts.

topics.title: Final accounts
topics.content: Final accounts: trading account, profit and loss, statement of financial position and adjustments.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: analyse each transaction, identify affected accounts, then apply debit and credit rules.

title: Geography Practice Guide
introduction: Use diagrams and maps where possible. Connect physical processes with the landforms and human activities they create. Use diagrams, maps and data. Learn to connect physical processes with the landforms and human activities they produce.

topics.title: Map Work
topics.content: Practise scale, bearings, direction, grid references, relief and interpretation of conventional signs.

topics.title: Physical Geography
topics.content: Revise weather, climate, rocks, rivers, erosion, coastal processes and natural vegetation.

topics.title: Human Geography
topics.content: Study population, settlement, agriculture, industry, transport, trade and environmental issues.

topics.title: Physical geography
topics.content: Physical geography: weather, climate, rocks, rivers, coasts, soils, vegetation and hazards.

topics.title: Human geography
topics.content: Human geography: population, settlement, migration, agriculture, industry, transport and urbanisation.

topics.title: Map work
topics.content: Map work: scale, direction, grid references, relief, contours, cross-sections and interpretation.

topics.title: Fieldwork
topics.content: Fieldwork: sampling, observation, measurement, presentation and evaluation of evidence.

title: Agricultural Science Guide
introduction: Combine practical farm knowledge with scientific principles governing crops, livestock and soils. Relate farm practices to productivity, sustainability and management. Use local examples when revising tropical agriculture.

topics.title: Soil Science
topics.content: Revise soil texture, structure, fertility, pH, erosion and methods of soil improvement.

topics.title: Crop Production
topics.content: Study propagation, nursery practices, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, storage and pests.

topics.title: Animal Production
topics.content: Revise breeds, nutrition, housing, disease prevention, reproduction and farm records.

topics.title: Crop production
topics.content: Crop production: soil preparation, planting, nutrition, weed/pest control, harvesting and storage.

topics.title: Animal production
topics.content: Animal production: breeds, feeding, housing, reproduction, health and management records.

topics.title: Farm management
topics.content: Farm management: budgeting, records, credit, marketing, labour and risk.

topics.title: Sustainable agriculture
topics.content: Sustainable agriculture: erosion control, crop rotation, organic matter, conservation and safe chemical use.

title: Literature-in-English Guide
introduction: Read beyond the plot. Examine character, conflict, theme, setting, language and dramatic or poetic techniques. Read widely and practise identifying literary devices from context. Support interpretations with evidence from the work being studied.

topics.title: Prose
topics.content: Practise identifying characterisation, themes, point of view, setting, symbolism and narrative techniques.

topics.title: Poetry
topics.content: Revise imagery, tone, mood, diction, rhyme, rhythm, figures of speech and the relationship between form and meaning.

topics.title: Drama
topics.content: Study plot development, dialogue, stage directions, conflict, dramatic irony and character motivation.

topics.title: Genres
topics.content: Genres: poetry, prose and drama; know their structural and performance features.

topics.title: Literary devices
topics.content: Literary devices: imagery, metaphor, simile, irony, symbolism, alliteration, diction and tone.

topics.title: Narrative technique
topics.content: Narrative technique: plot, characterisation, point of view, setting, conflict and theme.

topics.title: Practice routine
topics.content: Practice routine: identify the device, explain its effect, then connect it to meaning or character.

title: Civic Education Guide
introduction: Civic questions often test both definitions and the practical importance of values, rights and responsibilities. Civic questions often test both knowledge and application. Learn the principle, its purpose, and how citizens or institutions demonstrate it.

topics.title: Rights and Duties
topics.content: Revise fundamental rights, civic duties, responsibilities of citizens and lawful participation in society.

topics.title: Democratic Values
topics.content: Study justice, tolerance, accountability, integrity, rule of law, equality and respect for diversity.

topics.title: National Development
topics.content: Practise topics on national unity, corruption, leadership, responsible citizenship and community participation.

topics.title: Rights and responsibilities
topics.content: Rights and responsibilities: human rights, duties, rule of law, equality and justice.

topics.title: Democracy
topics.content: Democracy: elections, participation, accountability, public opinion and political institutions.

topics.title: National values
topics.content: National values: patriotism, tolerance, integrity, unity, hard work and respect for diversity.

topics.title: Social issues
topics.content: Social issues: corruption, environmental responsibility, conflict resolution, security and community development.
